editorNote: Regulators were the through-line today: a Polish competition charge against Google sits beside a US court win, while Strive's biggest weekly bitcoin purchase and gold's slide below $4,150 round out the tape. Disclosed facts only; nothing here is investment advice.

stories.headline: Strive buys 2,000 bitcoin for about $169 million and sets up a $500 million buyback for its SATA preferred
stories.summary: In an 8-K filed Oct. 5, Strive disclosed buying 2,000 bitcoin between Sept. 28 and Oct. 2 at an average of about $84,422, lifting holdings to 29,462 BTC. About 61.5% of the capital came from its SATA preferred stock, and the company also has a repurchase facility of up to $500 million for SATA.
stories.whyItMatters: It was Strive's largest weekly bitcoin purchase to date, and the new facility lets it buy back preferred stock as well as accumulate bitcoin.

stories.headline: Poland's competition watchdog charges Google over publisher payment talks, a week after a US court tossed AI-summary suits
stories.summary: Poland's UOKiK charged Google with possibly abusing its dominant position by proposing payments to publishers without giving them the data to assess the rates; the maximum penalty is 10% of turnover. Separately, on Oct. 1 a US judge dismissed Chegg and Penske Media suits claiming Google forced publishers to accept AI summaries.
stories.whyItMatters: Alphabet drew a formal European charge on the same news cycle that a US court rejected publisher claims over AI summaries; the stock traded near $345, up about 0.4%, in morning trading.

stories.headline: Gold sits near $4,135–$4,155, down about 6% over the past month
stories.summary: Spot gold traded around $4,134 per ounce at 10:33 a.m. ET on Oct. 5 per Kitco, with other quotes between about $4,138 and $4,158 depending on the venue and time. Trading Economics shows it down roughly 6% over the last month and 4.45% above a year ago.
stories.whyItMatters: Gold is holding in the low $4,100s after last week's slide, with quotes differing by a few dollars across data providers.

stories.headline: Alibaba insider filings: director Joseph Tsai's RSUs vest, and the CFO's tax-related sale trims his stake
stories.summary: A Form 4 shows director Joseph Tsai acquired 3,334 and 7,500 ordinary shares on Oct. 1 as restricted share units vested. Separately, CFO Hong Xu sold 103,046 shares worth about $1.41 million on Sept. 25, shares withheld and sold in Hong Kong to cover taxes on a vesting of 229,000 shares; he still holds 1,064,020.
stories.whyItMatters: Both are routine equity-award settlements rather than open-market bets; the filings add detail on insider holdings.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab slips as SpaceX climbs 5% on a reiterated Morgan Stanley $300 target
stories.summary: On Oct. 5 SpaceX shares rose about 5% as Musk renamed SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI and Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas reiterated an Overweight rating and $300 target; Rocket Lab shares slipped in the same session, per 24/7 Wall St.
stories.whyItMatters: Rocket Lab traded lower on a day its larger space peer rose, which shows the two stocks do not always move together.
